name: Norway
tagline: A country shaped by water that had somewhere to be.
summary: Norway is long — its coastline, unfolded, would wrap a good way round the world — and almost everything worth seeing sits where rock meets salt water. The interior is high plateau and slow trains; the coast is fjord, ferry and fishing town. Prices are the highest in Europe and the light is the strangest: midnight sun above the Arctic Circle in June, four-hour days in December.

season.note: June and July give you the midnight sun and open mountain roads. Late September brings colour and empty trails. Late January to March is the northern lights and ski season; November is neither.

getting_around: The Bergen and Dovre railways are two of Europe's great train rides and cost less than the equivalent flight if booked early. Coastal Norway runs on ferries and express boats — treat them as public transport, not excursions. North of Trondheim, distances get serious: fly, or take the coastal ferry and give it days rather than hours.
food: Brown cheese (brunost) — caramelised whey, sliced thin, an acquired and worthwhile taste
Cured and smoked salmon, and the fresher, less-famous cod
Kanelbolle: the cinnamon bun that fuels every hike

festivals.name: Midnight sun period
festivals.where: Everywhere north of the Arctic Circle

festivals.name: Northern Lights season begins in earnest

know: Card and phone payment work everywhere, including on ferries and in mountain huts. Cash is close to useless.
Allemannsretten — the right to roam — lets you walk and camp on uncultivated land, with obligations attached: no fires in summer, no trace, 150 metres from any house.
Alcohol above 4.7% is sold only in state Vinmonopolet shops, which close early and shut on Sundays.

regions.name: Østlandet & the East
regions.summary: The populated, farmed, forested east: the capital, the big lakes, and the valleys the ski world takes seriously.

cities.name: Oslo
cities.summary: A capital that spent its oil money on architecture and then put a forest and a fjord within a tram ride of the result.
highlights: The Munch museum and the National Museum, which between them hold the versions of The Scream worth arguing about
The Fram and Kon-Tiki polar ships, kept whole in Bygdøy
Island-hopping the inner Oslofjord on a standard public ferry ticket
Nordmarka: 1,700 km of forest trail, reached by metro

experiences.name: The commuter ferry as a day out
experiences.summary: Ride the public boats to Hovedøya and Gressholmen with a swim towel and a bakery bag; it is a city transport ticket, not a cruise.

experiences.name: Waterfront architecture walk
experiences.summary: Opera roof to Munch to the library at Bjørvika — twenty years of a city deciding what it wanted to look like, in ninety minutes.

places.name: MUNCH
places.summary: Thirteen floors on the waterfront holding the artist's own bequest — 26,000 works, including the versions of The Scream worth arguing about.

places.name: Fram Museum
places.summary: The polar ship Fram kept whole indoors, with her hull open so you can walk the decks that drifted across the Arctic for three years.

places.name: Vigeland Sculpture Park
places.summary: 212 bronze and granite figures by one sculptor in one park, free and open at every hour, including four in the morning.

places.name: Akershus Fortress
places.summary: A medieval castle on the harbour that was never taken by siege, with the government quarter and the fjord on either side of it.

places.name: Oslo Opera House
places.summary: A roof that comes down to the water so the public can walk up it, which is the building's actual argument.

cities.name: Lillehammer
cities.summary: Olympic town on a long lake, with an open-air museum that is really a village of 200 relocated buildings.
highlights: Maihaugen: farms, a stave church and a whole timber town, walked rather than viewed
The 1994 Olympic bob track, still rideable
Cross-country trails that start where the streets end

experiences.name: Maihaugen open-air museum
experiences.summary: Two hundred buildings moved log by log from across Gudbrandsdalen; the point is the carpentry, not the costumes.

places.name: Maihaugen
places.summary: Two hundred buildings moved log by log from across Gudbrandsdalen, including a stave church.

cities.name: Fredrikstad
cities.summary: Scandinavia's best-preserved fortress town, on an island in a river mouth, reached by a free ferry.
highlights: Gamlebyen: ramparts, moat and cobbles, still inhabited
The free city ferry, which is public transport and runs all day
Hvaler's skerries, an hour south by bus and boat

experiences.name: The free ferry, all day
experiences.summary: Fredrikstad runs its river crossings free of charge as ordinary transport; ride them between the old town and the new for as long as you like.

cities.name: Rjukan
cities.summary: A company town in a gorge so deep the sun does not reach it for six months, so the town installed mirrors on the mountain.
highlights: The sun mirrors on Gvepseborg, throwing daylight into the square since 2013
Vemork: the heavy water plant sabotaged in 1943, now a museum
Gaustatoppen, and the tram inside the mountain built for NATO

experiences.name: Vemork and the heavy water raid
experiences.summary: The plant, the pipeline the saboteurs climbed, and an account that does not tidy up how close it came to failing.

places.name: Vemork
places.summary: The heavy water plant sabotaged in 1943, with the pipeline the saboteurs climbed still on the cliff.

places.name: The Sun Mirrors
places.summary: Three heliostats on the mountain throwing daylight into a square the sun cannot reach for six months.

regions.name: Sørlandet & the South Coast
regions.summary: White wooden towns on a skerry coast, where Norway goes on holiday and almost no foreign visitor does.

cities.name: Kristiansand
cities.summary: A grid-planned town on the warmest stretch of Norwegian coast, with a bathing park in the middle of it.
highlights: Posebyen's white timber quarter, 200 years of it
Bystranda, a city beach that is genuinely used
Ferries out to the skerries all summer

cities.name: Risør
cities.summary: 'The white town by the Skagerrak' — 300 wooden houses round a harbour, and a wooden boat festival each August.
highlights: The wooden boat festival, the largest in the Nordics
Stangholmen lighthouse island, twenty minutes by boat
Craft workshops in the old warehouses

experiences.name: The wooden boat festival
experiences.summary: Every August the harbour fills with clinker-built boats and the people who maintain them; go for the sound of the hulls rather than the programme.

cities.name: Lindesnes
cities.summary: Norway's southernmost point, with a lighthouse on it and a restaurant five metres under the sea beside it.
highlights: The lighthouse, lit since 1656
Under: a dining room submerged against the seabed
2,518 km to the North Cape, in a straight line north

regions.name: Fjord Norway
regions.summary: The west coast: Bergen and its rain, the deep fjord arms, and the roads that only open when the snow lets them.

cities.name: Bergen
cities.summary: A hanseatic trading port wedged between seven mountains, wet 200 days a year and entirely unbothered about it.
highlights: Bryggen's leaning wooden warehouses, and the fire history that explains their gaps
The Fløibanen funicular to a mountain you can walk down in an hour
The fish market — better one street back, where the locals buy
The Bergen Railway east: seven hours across a high plateau

experiences.name: Fløyen to Ulriken ridge walk
experiences.summary: Five hours along the tops between the two cable cars, with the city on one side and nothing but bog and rock on the other.

experiences.name: Lunch at a working fish counter
experiences.summary: Skip the tourist stalls; eat where the boats deliver, standing up, whatever came in that morning.

places.name: Bryggen
places.summary: The leaning wooden trading houses of the Hanseatic wharf, rebuilt after each fire on the same foundations since the 1100s.

places.name: Fløyen
places.summary: 320 metres above the city by funicular, with a path down through the woods that most people forget to take.

places.name: Fish Market
places.summary: Outdoor from May, indoors year-round, and better one street back where the boats actually deliver.

places.name: KODE
places.summary: Four buildings on one street holding Munch, Astrup and the largest Norwegian art collection outside Oslo.

cities.name: Flåm
cities.summary: A hamlet at the end of a fjord arm, famous for a railway that drops 865 metres in twenty kilometres.
highlights: The Flåm Railway, best taken uphill and walked or cycled back down
Nærøyfjord: a UNESCO-listed fjord arm 250 metres wide at its narrowest
Aurlandsdalen, a day-long valley walk between old summer farms

experiences.name: Ride the Rallarvegen down
experiences.summary: The old navvies' road from Myrdal, gravel all the way, downhill nearly all the way — a bike, a train ticket and a whole afternoon.

places.name: Flåm Railway
places.summary: Twenty kilometres and 865 metres of descent through twenty tunnels, most of them dug by hand.

places.name: Nærøyfjord
places.summary: A UNESCO fjord arm 250 metres wide at its narrowest, with waterfalls straight off the wall above the boat.

cities.name: Ålesund
cities.summary: Burned to the ground in 1904 and rebuilt, all at once, in Art Nouveau — so the whole town matches.
highlights: 418 steps up Aksla for the archipelago laid out below
The Jugendstil centre, in the old pharmacy
Day boats to Runde's puffin cliffs in early summer

experiences.name: The town that burned and matched
experiences.summary: A short walk that only works once you know the date: every façade you pass was drawn in the same three years.

places.name: Aksla
places.summary: 418 steps up from the town park, with the Art Nouveau roofs and the archipelago laid out below.

places.name: Jugendstilsenteret
places.summary: The Art Nouveau centre in the old pharmacy, explaining why an entire town matches.

cities.name: Stavanger
cities.summary: Oil capital with a preserved wooden old town, and the most photographed cliff in Norway an hour away.
highlights: Gamle Stavanger: 173 white wooden houses from the 18th century
Preikestolen, a 604-metre flat cliff, four hours there and back
The Norwegian Petroleum Museum, which is franker about the industry than you expect

experiences.name: Preikestolen, early
experiences.summary: Eight kilometres round on rock and boardwalk. Start before seven; by eleven there is a queue for the photograph and no railing to queue behind.

places.name: Preikestolen
places.summary: A flat slab 604 metres above the Lysefjord with no railing, reached by an eight-kilometre path.

places.name: Gamle Stavanger
places.summary: 173 white wooden houses from the 18th and 19th centuries, on cobbled lanes above the harbour.

places.name: Norwegian Petroleum Museum
places.summary: The industry that paid for modern Norway, explained more frankly than a national museum usually manages.

cities.name: Odda & Trolltunga
cities.summary: A smelter town at the end of a fjord arm, and a slab of rock that sticks 700 metres out over a lake.
highlights: Trolltunga: 28 km round, ten hours, and not a stroll
Folgefonna glacier above the valley
The smelter town itself, which is on the UNESCO tentative list and is not pretty

experiences.name: Trolltunga, with the day it needs
experiences.summary: Ten to twelve hours, a 1,200-metre climb, and mountain rescue callouts every season from people who read it as a viewpoint with a car park.

cities.name: Voss
cities.summary: A lake town between two fjords that decided to become Norway's outdoor sports capital and succeeded.
highlights: Skydiving, paragliding and rafting, all within the town
The Bergen Railway stops here, which is how everyone arrives
Ski country twenty minutes up the mountain

cities.name: Geiranger
cities.summary: A UNESCO fjord arm 15 km long with waterfalls falling straight into it and abandoned farms on ledges above.
highlights: The Seven Sisters falls, and the farm ruins on shelves opposite
Dalsnibba, 1,500 metres, with the fjord directly below
The Trollstigen road north, eleven hairpins with a wall on one side

experiences.name: The farms on the ledges
experiences.summary: Skageflå was farmed until 1918 on a shelf 250 metres above the water, reached by ladder. The boat drops you at the bottom and you climb.

places.name: The Seven Sisters
places.summary: Seven falls dropping 250 metres into the fjord, opposite a suitor who never got anywhere.

places.name: Skageflå
places.summary: A farm worked until 1918 on a ledge 250 metres above the water, reached by boat and then by climbing.

cities.name: Balestrand
cities.summary: A Sognefjord village of dragon-style timber villas, where 19th-century painters came and then stayed.
highlights: Dragestil villas, a Norwegian national-romantic invention
The English church of St Olaf, built by a homesick Englishwoman in 1897
Express boats along the longest fjord in Norway

regions.name: Trøndelag
regions.summary: The old seat of Norwegian kings, plus a copper town preserved by being too remote to modernise.

cities.name: Trondheim
cities.summary: A student city built around the northernmost medieval cathedral in the world, and the end of a thousand-year pilgrim path.
highlights: Nidaros Cathedral, the terminus of the St Olav Ways
The old wharves along the Nidelva, best from the Gamle Bybro
A food scene punching far above a city of 200,000

experiences.name: The cathedral, from the workshop side
experiences.summary: The stoneyard has been cutting replacement blocks continuously for a century; see that before you see the nave.

places.name: Nidaros Cathedral
places.summary: The northernmost medieval cathedral in the world, the end of the St Olav Ways, and a stoneyard that has cut replacement blocks continuously for a century.

places.name: Gamle Bybro
places.summary: The old town bridge, red-painted, with the wooden wharves of the Nidelva on both sides of it.

places.name: Ringve Music Museum
places.summary: A national collection of musical instruments in a manor house above the fjord, played rather than displayed.

cities.name: Røros
cities.summary: A 17th-century copper-mining town of black timber houses, at -30°C for weeks at a stretch and listed by UNESCO for surviving intact.
highlights: Slaggveien: turf-roofed miners' cottages on slag heaps
The mine at Olavsgruva, 50 metres underground
Røros Martnan, the February winter market

experiences.name: Down the Olav mine
experiences.summary: Five degrees underground year-round, hard hats, and the noise a hand drill made before compressed air.

places.name: Røros Church
places.summary: A 1784 stone church seating 1,600 in a town of 3,700, built by a copper company for its workers.

places.name: Olavsgruva Mine
places.summary: Fifty metres underground at five degrees year-round, in a copper mine worked from 1650.

places.name: Slaggveien
places.summary: Turf-roofed miners' cottages built on the slag heaps, which is the whole social history in one lane.

regions.name: Northern Norway
regions.summary: Above the Arctic Circle: island chains, Sámi country, whales in winter and no darkness at all in June.

cities.name: Tromsø
cities.summary: A university town at 69°N with more bars per head than anywhere else in Norway, and the aurora directly overhead.
highlights: The Arctic Cathedral and the cable car above the strait
Aurora hunting between late September and late March, inland where the sky is clearer
Whale watching off Skjervøy in November and December

experiences.name: An aurora night with a forecast, not a promise
experiences.summary: A guide who drives to clear sky — sometimes into Finland — is worth more than one who stays put; nobody can guarantee the lights, and anyone who does is selling something.

experiences.name: A Sámi reindeer herding afternoon
experiences.summary: Book with a Sámi-owned operator; the difference between a working herd and a photo backdrop is obvious within ten minutes.

places.name: Arctic Cathedral
places.summary: Eleven concrete triangles and a glass mosaic 23 metres high, finished in 1965 and visible from the whole city.

places.name: Polaria
places.summary: A small aquarium and Arctic research centre with bearded seals, built as five ice floes tipped against a shore.

places.name: Storsteinen
places.summary: 421 metres by cable car, with the island city below and the midnight sun above it from late May.

cities.name: Lofoten (Svolvær)
cities.summary: Granite peaks that rise straight from the sea, red fishermen's cabins below them, and cod drying on racks every spring.
highlights: Reine and Hamnøy, the two views that put Lofoten on every screen
Ryten and Reinebringen — short, steep, and worth the calves
Sleeping in a rorbu, the cabins built for seasonal cod crews
Unstad's cold-water surf, wetsuits mandatory

experiences.name: A night in a working rorbu
experiences.summary: The old cod-fishing cabins on stilts; the good ones still smell faintly of tar and are still owned by fishing families.

experiences.name: Cold-water surf at Unstad
experiences.summary: Beach break inside the Arctic Circle, 6mm of neoprene, and a sauna afterwards that you will remember longer than the waves.

places.name: Reinebringen
places.summary: 1,566 Sherpa-built stone steps to the view of Reine that appears on every poster of Norway.

places.name: Unstad
places.summary: A cold-water surf break inside the Arctic Circle, with a sauna at the top of the sand.

places.name: Lofotr Viking Museum
places.summary: A reconstructed 83-metre chieftain's longhouse on the site where the original was found in a barley field.

cities.name: Bodø
cities.summary: A rebuilt northern port with the strongest tidal current in the world at its door and Lofoten across the water.
highlights: Saltstraumen: 400 million cubic metres of water through a 150-metre strait, four times a day
The coastal ferry and the Lofoten crossing
Sea eagles, which are ordinary here

experiences.name: Saltstraumen at full flow
experiences.summary: Check the tide table and stand on the bridge: whirlpools ten metres across, and fishermen working the edge of them.

cities.name: Narvik
cities.summary: An ice-free ore port at the end of a Swedish railway, ringed by mountains that drop into the fjord.
highlights: The Ofoten Railway to Kiruna, built for iron ore in 1902
The war museum, on a town fought over for two months in 1940
A cable car from the town centre to 656 metres

cities.name: Senja
cities.summary: Norway's second-largest island — Lofoten's landscape without Lofoten's traffic, and almost no one on the trails.
highlights: Segla and Hesten: short, steep, and among the best views in the country
Fishing villages on the outer coast with working boats
A national scenic route with rest stops designed by architects

cities.name: Alta
cities.summary: Finnmark's largest town, with 6,000-year-old rock carvings and a cathedral shaped like the aurora.
highlights: Hjemmeluft's rock art, on the UNESCO list, walked on boardwalks
The Northern Lights Cathedral, a titanium spiral
The Finnmarksløpet, Europe's longest sled dog race, in March

experiences.name: Six thousand years of rock carving
experiences.summary: Thousands of figures — boats, reindeer, bears, people — pecked into coastal rock over five millennia, and read in order along a boardwalk.

cities.name: Nordkapp (Honningsvåg)
cities.summary: A cliff at 71°N sold as the top of Europe, on an island reached by tunnel, with a fishing town below it.
highlights: The plateau at midnight in June, with the sun still up
Gjesvær's bird cliffs: puffins, gannets and 100,000 pairs
Honningsvåg itself, which is a working port and better company than the cape

regions.name: Svalbard
regions.summary: An Arctic archipelago at 78°N, with more polar bears than people and a treaty that lets anyone live there.

cities.name: Longyearbyen
cities.summary: The world's northernmost town of any size: a coal settlement turned research station, where leaving the settlement requires a rifle.
highlights: Polar night from late October to mid-February, and midnight sun from April
The global seed vault, seen from outside only
Rules that are not tourism theatre: bear watch outside town is a legal requirement
Old mining infrastructure left where it stands, because nothing rots up here

experiences.name: Out of town, legally
experiences.summary: Any trip beyond the settlement needs a guide carrying a rifle and trained to avoid using it. That is the law and it is also the honest reading of the risk.

experiences.name: Dog sledding on the glacier
experiences.summary: Wheeled carts in summer, runners in winter, and the same dogs that supplied the mines before snowmobiles.

places.name: Svalbard Museum
places.summary: Whaling, mining, trapping and the ecology of an archipelago where nothing decomposes, in one well-made room.

places.name: Global Seed Vault
places.summary: A concrete wedge in a mountainside holding a million seed samples. Nobody goes inside; the point is that it is there.
